evidence.claim: The old courthouse in Montross was a place where events elsewhere in the colony prompted local political action.
evidence.quote: The Old Westmoreland Court House in Montross was the site of notable events in 1774–1775 connected with the Revolutionary War.

evidence.claim: The old courthouse in Montross was a place where events elsewhere in the colony prompted local political action. A courthouse marker records that a meeting on June 22, 1774, adopted Richard Henry Lee’s resolution to aid Boston after Britain blockaded the port. The next year, Royal Governor Lord Dunmore’s seizure of gunpowder in Williamsburg prompted the Westmoreland Committee of Safety to meet here on May 23. The committee denounced the governor’s actions in another resolution. Kings Highway passes east of the historic courthouse as it turns through the center of the county seat.
evidence.quote: It is the county seat of Westmoreland County.

evidence.claim: A courthouse marker records that a meeting on June 22, 1774, adopted Richard Henry Lee’s resolution to aid Boston after Britain blockaded the port.
evidence.quote: According to a historic marker at the courthouse, a resolution was introduced by Richard Henry Lee and adopted at a meeting there on June 22, 1774, providing aid to Boston, Massachusetts, following a blockade of that beleaguered port city by Great Britain.

evidence.claim: The next year, Royal Governor Lord Dunmore’s seizure of gunpowder in Williamsburg prompted the Westmoreland Committee of Safety to meet here on May 23.
evidence.quote: The seizure in 1775 of the Virginia Colony's gunpowder supply in Williamsburg on orders of the Royal Governor, in what became known as the Gunpowder Incident, prompted the Westmoreland Committee of Safety to convene at the Court House on May 23, 1775.

evidence.claim: The committee denounced the governor’s actions in another resolution.
evidence.quote: The committee passed a resolution denouncing the governor, Lord Dunmore, for his actions.
